scope: Operative philology — philology that DOES something. Not description of texts but operations ON them: instruments, transforms, reconstructions, decompressions, collations that act. Plus operative semiotics, poetics and lyric theory.

claims.note: 'Operative' is the load-bearing word: philology that operates. A census, a collation, a transform spec, a reconstruction protocol are all Grammata work. A poem is not — that is NH2.

inaugural_issue.rationale: Opens on Sigil's own sigillographic foundations (#42), then Socrates as Orthonym (#123) and the Abraham Principle (#99) as the two constitutive-one operators, the Prophetic Catalog (#83) and Matthew 25 formalized (#8) as scriptural operation, The Future Beloved (#134) for lyric address as temporal projection, Counterfeit Orthodoxies (#65) for the citation map, and Sémantique Potentielle (#46) as the constraint-based mint. The through-line: every piece OPERATES on a text rather than describing one.
